Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

threaten verb

someone, with something

also threatening, make threats, threaten to, menace, have it in for someone

classical

Cic. Tusc. 1.102: crucem minārī alicui (Lewis & Short)
Sall. Cat. 23.3: minārī interdum ferrō

minor, minārī, minātus sum

verb, first conjugation, deponent: the person in the dative, the threat in the accusative or ablative

The person threatened is in the dative (mihi minātur), the threat in the accusative or the ablative. “Threaten to do” is accusative and infinitive: minātus sēsē abīre (Plaut. As. 3.3.14). Properly, of rocks, to jut out (Verg. A. 1.162).

Other words

  • minitor, minitārī, minitātus sum — keep threatening, threaten roundly

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Plaut. Curc. 4.4.15 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Phil. 6.10: frātrī mortem minitārī

    The frequentative of minor, common in comedy and in Cicero, with the same constructions.

Examples

  • Mihin' malum minitāre?

    Are you threatening me?Plaut. Curc. 4.4.15 (Lewis & Short)

  • Nōlī frātrī minārī.

    Don’t threaten your brother.composed

  • alicui perīculum dēnūntiāre

    to threaten someone, have it in for someoneTraupman 326

See also threat, threaten, warn, frighten.

SourcesLewis & Short: minor · Lewis & Short: minitor

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 326.
